facts.statement: Chuanqilong lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous

facts.statement: The genus Chuanqilong was described by Han et al. in 2014.
facts.quote: authority: Han et al., 2014

facts.statement: The type species of Chuanqilong is Chuanqilong chaoyangensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Chuanqilong chaoyangensis

facts.statement: Chuanqilong lived between 124.0 and 121 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: lived during the Early Cretaceous ( Barremian to Aptian stage, 124.0 to 121 Ma)

facts.statement: Fossils of Chuanqilong were found in the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: in what is now the Jiufotang Formation

facts.statement: Chuanqilong was described in 2014 by Fenglu Han, Wenjie Zheng, Dongyu Hu, Xing Xu, and Paul M. Barrett.
facts.quote: It was described in 2014 by Fenglu Han, Wenjie Zheng, Dongyu Hu, Xing Xu, and Paul M. Barrett

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Chuanqilong may represent a later growth stage of Liaoningosaurus.
facts.quote: Chuanqilong shows many similarities with Liaoningosaurus and may represent a later ontogenetic stage of the taxon

facts.statement: Chuanqilong had a triangular skull and a neck protected by bands of osteoderms called cervical half rings.
facts.quote: It had a triangular skull and a neck that was protected by bands of osteoderms known as cervical half rings

facts.statement: Unlike more advanced ankylosaurids, Chuanqilong did not have a club at the end of its tail.
facts.quote: Unlike derived ankylosaurids, the end of its tail lacked a club

facts.statement: Chuanqilong was a quadruped with robust forelimbs and hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Like other ankylosaurids, it was quadrupedal with robust forelimbs and hindlimbs

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton of Chuanqilong was collected by local farmers from a quarry in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: A nearly complete skeleton was collected by local farmers from a single quarry in the Liaoning Province, China

facts.statement: The skeleton was recovered from the Jiufotang Formation, dating to 122.0 to 118.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: The skeleton was recovered from the Jiufotang Formation which dates to the late Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous period, 122.0 to 118.9 Ma

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, CJPM V001, is a nearly complete skull and skeleton representing a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, CJPM V001, consists of a nearly complete skull and skeleton, with only the distal portion of the caudal series missing, and represents a juvenile individual

facts.statement: The type specimen is housed at the Chaoyang Jizantang Paleontological Museum.
facts.quote: The type specimen is currently housed at the Chaoyang Jizantang Paleontological Museum

facts.statement: The name Chuanqilong comes from Chinese words meaning "legendary" and "dragon".
facts.quote: The generic name, Chuanqilong, is derived from the Chinese words "Chuanqi" (legendary), in reference to the abundance of fossils of western Liaoning, and "long" (dragon)

facts.statement: The specific name chaoyangensis refers to the geographical area of Chaoyang.
facts.quote: The specific name, chaoyangensis, refers to the broader geographical area which encompasses the type locality

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Chuanqilong holotype represents an adult or a juvenile, with some researchers suggesting it might be an adult Liaoningosaurus.
facts.quote: A Canadian Society of Vertebrate Palaeontology abstract book that was published in 2019 mentioned that the type and only known specimen of Chuanqilong actually represented an adult individual, in contrast to the interpretation of Han et al. (2014), and may have been Liaoningosaurus at a different and later ontogenetic stage

facts.statement: The original description estimated Chuanqilong's length at 4.5 meters (14.8 feet).
facts.quote: Han et al. (2014) gave Chuanqilong an estimated length of 4.5 metres (14.8 feet)

facts.statement: Another unique trait is that the distally tapering ischium is constricted at its midshaft.
facts.quote: The distally tapering ischium is constricted at midshaft length

facts.statement: Other unique traits include a long retroarticular process, a slender wedge-like lacrimal, and a humerus-to-femur length ratio of 0.88.
facts.quote: Other distinguishing traits include the presence of a long retroarticular process, the presence of a lacrimal that is slender and wedge-like, a ratio of humerus to femur length of 0.88

facts.statement: In ventral view, the skull of Chuanqilong is triangular.
facts.quote: In ventral view, the skull is triangular

facts.statement: Unlike nodosaurids, the quadrate in Chuanqilong is not fused with the squamosal.
facts.quote: Unlike nodosaurids, the quadrate isn't fused with the squamosal

facts.statement: Like most ankylosaurs, the medial condyle is wider and extends further downwards than the lateral condyle.
facts.quote: As in most other ankylosaurs, the medial condyle is wider across and extends further towards the underside than the lateral condyle

facts.statement: Preserved rostral maxillary teeth are smaller than caudal teeth, with crowns as tall as they are wide and swollen bases.
facts.quote: The rostral maxillary teeth that are preserved are smaller than the caudal teeth, with their crowns being as tall as they are wide and their bases being swollen with a weak cingulum

facts.statement: The mandible is long and shallow, similar to other basal ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: The mandible is similar to that of other basal ankylosaurids as it is long and shallow

facts.statement: Unlike other basal ankylosaurids, the mandible lacks an osteoderm on its underside margin.
facts.quote: However, it lacks an osteoderm on the underside margin unlike other basal ankylosaurids

facts.statement: The dentary tooth row is straight and less sinusoidal than that of derived ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: The dentary tooth row is not as strongly sinusoidal as those of derived ankylosaurs and is straight

facts.statement: Chuanqilong lacked a tail club because it did not have modified handle-like vertebrae at the end of its tail.
facts.quote: Unlike other ankylosaurids, Chuanqilong lacked a tail club as it lacks the modified handle-like vertebrae in the distal portion of the tail.

facts.statement: The coracoid of Chuanqilong was not fused to the scapula, a feature that may indicate it was a juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: The coracoid is not co-ossified with the scapula, which might represent an ontogenetic trait as it is also known in other juvenile ankylosaur specimens.

facts.statement: Chuanqilong possessed a wedge-shaped olecranon process on the ulna, which may be an ontogenetic trait seen in immature ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: The ulna has a wedge-shaped olecranon process, as in other immature ankylosaur specimens and may represent an ontogenetic characteristic.

facts.statement: The ischium of Chuanqilong was long, lacked an obturator process, and had a slender shaft curving slightly downward.
facts.quote: The ischium is long, lacks an obturator process and has a slender shaft that curves slightly towards the underside.

facts.statement: The preserved cervical half ring of Chuanqilong is a single fused plate compressed dorsally and ventrally, segmented into four sections.
facts.quote: The only preserved cervical half ring of Chuanqilong consists of a connecting band that is fused into a single plate, but is compressed towards the dorsal and ventral sides and is also segmented into four sections.

facts.statement: The shoulder region of Chuanqilong preserves two large, flat, thickened osteoderm plates with a subrectangular outline.
facts.quote: The shoulder region preserves two osteoderm plates that are large, flat, thickened and have a subrectangular outline.

facts.statement: Small and irregular osteoderms and ossicles were preserved across the entire body of Chuanqilong.
facts.quote: Preserved over the entirety of the body are a diverse range of osteoderms and ossicles that are small and irregular.

facts.statement: Han et al. (2014) classified Chuanqilong as a basal ankylosaurid and the sister taxon to Liaoningosaurus.
facts.quote: Han et al. (2014) originally found Chuanqilong to be a basal ankylosaurid that was sister taxon to Liaoningosaurus.

facts.statement: Frauenfelder et al. (2022) recovered Chuanqilong in a clade with Liaoningosaurus and Cedarpelta, outside the families Ankylosauridae and Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Frauenfelder et al. (2022) found Chuanqilong to be within a clade including Liaoningosaurus and Cedarpelta outside of Ankylosauridae and Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: A 2019 abstract suggested that Chuanqilong and Liaoningosaurus might be the same species at different growth stages.
facts.quote: In 2019, an abstract suggested the possibility that Chuanqilong and Liaoningosaurus may represent the same species but at different ontogenetic stages.

facts.statement: Fossils of Chuanqilong were found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning Province, China.
